prompt:
You are given a region of the natural-language text of a mathematics paper, shown
as numbered lines `@OFFSET|text` (the `@OFFSET|` prefix is a reading aid, NOT part
of the text). Split this region into its parts, in reading order, so they cover the
whole region with no gaps, and label each part.

Label each part with EXACTLY ONE of the allowed label-paths below — copy it
VERBATIM, including the dots (e.g. `formula.compound-formula.quantified.universal`).
These are the only labels valid at this position:
  - definition
  - theorem
  - organizer-section
  - commentary

Load-bearing rules for choosing the label:
  - commentary : use ONLY if you are CERTAIN this part contains NO formal content
      (no definition, theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary, proof, or formal
      statement) and is pure natural-language connective tissue — motivation,
      transitions, remarks, references/bibliography. A `commentary` part is
      TERMINAL: it is never explored further, so any formal content hidden inside
      is LOST. If you are not CERTAIN it is purely non-formal, do NOT use commentary.
  - organizer-section (only if it appears above) : a structural/section container,
      OR ANY part you are not certain how to classify. This is the SAFE DEFAULT —
      "unsure ⇒ organizer-section" — because it will be explored (split) further.
  - the remaining labels are standard mathematical-structure roles (e.g. definition,
      theorem, proof, statement, conclusion, formula, tactic, …). Pick the one that
      fits this part. Only choose from the allowed list above.

Rule of thumb: the only error that loses information is calling something
`commentary` when it isn't. When in doubt, prefer `organizer-section` if offered,
otherwise the closest formal label — never `commentary`.

Output ONLY a JSON array (first char `[`, last char `]`, no prose). Each element:
{
  "label": "<one of the allowed labels>",
  "start_text": "<EXACT verbatim text at the START of this part, copied
     character-for-character from the lines (NOT including the @OFFSET| prefix),
     about 4–12 words — enough to locate this part's beginning uniquely>"
}

- Parts in reading order; the FIRST begins at the very start of the region.
- `start_text` must be an EXACT substring so it can be located by search.
